newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Hesse-Germany faces uphill EMU battle.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Hesse-Germany faces uphill EMU battle.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said on Monday that Germany would face difficulties reaching the three percent deficit goal for currency union unless new funds were found through other means.
"Without additional measures it will be difficult for Germany to meet the three percent deficit goal," Hesse said in the text of a speech.
Germany's Finance Minister Theo Waigel has said it would be necessary for a nation's deficits to be no higher than 3.0 percent in order to join the currency union.
On the other hand Hesse supported a strict interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty entry criteria and opposed any efforts to soften the criteria as part of a bid to help secure Germany's entery.
But Hesse, who is president of the state central bank in Lower Saxony, Saxony Anhalt and Bremen, also said it would be hard to imagine a currency union without Germany.
